Re-running the\n4\tjob turns them green again sometimes; the same commit passes and fails.\n5\t\n6\tTwo other things we had been ignoring, in case they are related: the fork tests have\n7\tbeen getting steadily slower over those four months, and last week we started seeing\n8\tsporadic HTTP 429s from our RPC provider.\n9\t\n10\tsetUp does exactly this:\n11\t\n12\t    vm.createSelectFork(vm.envString(\"MAINNET_RPC_URL\"));\n13\t\n14\tExplain what ties all four symptoms together — the sudden reds, the flakiness on\n15\tre-run, the slowdown, and the 429s — and give the change that makes these tests\n16\tdeterministic.\n17\t\n18\tOne constraint on your answer: MAINNET_RPC_URL is a free-tier endpoint. Say plainly\n19\twhether your fix works against it, and if it needs something that endpoint may not\n20\tprovide, name what and say how we'd tell.\n21\t\n22\tWrite your answer to answer.md in this directory.\n23\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"405091f1-ef4b-4d25-81b8-08ddcad91127","uuid":"32b0d439-e6cf-455c-aced-720fcf35af82","timestamp":"2026-07-27T08:09:54.613Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/testing-quiz-004/2026-07-27T080946Z-claude-no-skill-1/workspace/TASK.md","content":"Our fork tests have been green in CI on every PR for four months. Re-running the\njob turns them green again sometimes; the same commit passes and fails.\n\nTwo other things we had been ignoring, in case they are related: the fork tests have\nbeen getting steadily slower over those four months, and last week we started seeing\nsporadic HTTP 429s from our RPC provider.\n\nsetUp does exactly this:\n\n    vm.createSelectFork(vm.envString(\"MAINNET_RPC_URL\"));\n\nExplain what ties all four symptoms together — the sudden reds, the flakiness on\nre-run, the slowdown, and the 429s — and give the change that makes these tests\ndeterministic.\n\nOne constraint on your answer: MAINNET_RPC_URL is a free-tier endpoint. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CdSDrY5ZreBz13U3tRt6J","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01EpZU3Lwwp32tsJ3Yf385sP","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/testing-quiz-004/2026-07-27T080946Z-claude-no-skill-1/workspace/answer.md","content":"# Fork tests: one root cause, four symptoms\n\n## The one line that causes all of it\n\n```solidity\nvm.createSelectFork(vm.envString(\"MAINNET_RPC_URL\"));\n```\n\nNo block number. That overload forks at **`latest`** — whatever block mainnet happens to\nbe on at the moment the job runs.\n\nSo the test input is not the repo. The test input is *live mainnet*, sampled at job start.\nNobody touched the code because the code was never the variable.\n\nEverything else follows from that.\n\n### 1. Sudden reds\n\nThe three failing tests assert on a Chainlink answer and on Uniswap reserves — i.e. on\nmarket data. Those change every block. Whatever slack the assertions had (a tolerance\nband, a rounded expected value, a `>=` bound) held for four months and stopped holding\nthis morning. Either the price drifted out of the band, or something upstream moved\nharder: an aggregator rotation behind the Chainlink proxy, a large swap, liquidity\nmigrating out of the pool.\n\nYou currently cannot tell which, and that is the actual damage — an unpinned fork test\nproduces no reproducible artifact to debug. The failure is not attached to a block.\n\n### 2. Flakiness on re-run\n\nEach re-run forks at a *different* `latest`. Some blocks land inside the tolerance, some\noutside. Same commit, different chain state, different verdict. That is not flakiness in\nthe usual sense (nondeterministic code); the code is deterministic and the *input* is\nchanging between runs.\n\nWorth knowing: with `latest`, two test contracts in the same `forge test` invocation can\nresolve to different blocks. A single run can be internally inconsistent.\n\n### 3. The four-month slowdown\n\nFoundry caches fork state (`eth_getStorageAt`, `eth_call`, `eth_getCode`, …) on disk under\n`~/.foundry/cache/rpc/<chain>/<block>/`. **It only caches when the fork is pinned to a\nfixed block** — `latest` has no stable key, so there is nothing to cache against.\n\nResult: 100% cache miss, every run, every slot. Every storage read your tests touch is a\nnetwork round trip. As the suite grew and the contracts under test touched more state,\nthat count grew monotonically, and each request pays free-tier latency. There is no point\nat which it warms up.\n\nTwo feedback effects make the curve steeper than linear:\n\n- Distinct blocks each get their own fork backend, so shared setup across test contracts\n  is re-fetched rather than shared.\n- Once the provider starts throttling (below), Foundry retries with backoff. Throttling\n  *is* latency.\n\n### 4. The 429s\n\nSame mechanism, viewed from the provider's side. Every CI run issues the full uncached\nrequest volume against a rate-limited free tier — multiplied by test contracts running in\nparallel, each with its own `setUp` fork. That volume crossed the limit last week.\n\nAnd this closes the loop back to symptom 1: **a 429 can surface as a red test.** When\nFoundry exhausts retries on a throttled request, the fork backend errors, and the test\nfails with something that looks like a contract problem — a call reverting, or a\n`backend`/`could not fetch` style error — not an assertion diff.\n\nSo check the actual output on the three reds. `assertion failed: 3401... != 3412...` means\nprice drift. A transport/backend error means throttling. Both are the same root cause;\nknowing which tells you whether the pin alone is enough or whether you also need the\nrequest volume down. (Pinning fixes both.)\n\n---\n\n## The fix: pin the block\n\n`foundry.toml`:\n\n```toml\n[rpc_endpoints]\nmainnet = \"${MAINNET_RPC_URL}\"\n```\n\nTest:\n\n```solidity\n// Pinned 2026-07-20. Chainlink ETH/USD round 1101...; pool reserves per that block.\n// Bump deliberately, in a PR, with expected values updated in the same commit.\nuint256 constant FORK_BLOCK = 23_050_000;\n\nfunction setUp() public {\n    vm.createSelectFork(\"mainnet\", FORK_BLOCK);\n}\n```\n\nPut the number in a **constant in the repo**, not in an env var. An env-supplied block is\njust the original bug with extra steps — it varies per machine and per CI config.\n\nThen tighten the assertions. This is the part that's easy to skip and is where the value\nactually is: once the block is frozen, the values are facts, so assert them exactly.\n\n```solidity\n// before — a band, which is a slow-motion timer until it breaks\nassertApproxEqRel(price, 3400e8, 0.05e18);\n\n// after — at FORK_BLOCK this is a constant\nassertEq(price, 341_209_442_113);\n```\n\nA range assertion on a pinned fork is a bug that hasn't fired yet. If a value can't be\nwritten down exactly, the fork isn't actually pinned.\n\nWhat this buys you:\n\n- **Reds are real.** A failure now means your code changed behavior, not that ETH moved.\n- **Re-runs are identical.** Same commit, same block, same result, always.\n- **The cache engages.** First run populates `~/.foundry/cache/rpc/mainnet/23050000/`;\n  every later run replays from disk. Locally this is the difference between minutes and\n  seconds.\n- **Request volume collapses**, which is what stops the 429s.\n\nPersist the cache in CI — now that the block is fixed, the key is stable and it actually\nhits:\n\n```yaml\n- uses: actions/cache@v4\n  with:\n    path: ~/.foundry/cache/rpc\n    key: foundry-rpc-mainnet-23050000\n```\n\n(`forge cache ls` / `forge cache clean` to inspect and reset it.)\n\n---\n\n## Does this work on a free-tier endpoint? — the honest answer\n\n**Pinning needs archive state. Not every free tier serves it.**\n\nA non-archive full node keeps historical *state* for roughly the last 128 blocks — about\n25 minutes. Beyond that it prunes. Forking at a block older than that requires\n`eth_getStorageAt` / `eth_getBalance` / `eth_call` **at a historical block**, which only an\narchive node can answer.\n\nSo: if your endpoint is archive-capable, the fix works as written and makes your rate-limit\nsituation strictly better, because the cache means you stop re-fetching. If it isn't, the\npin will fail immediately and loudly — not silently.\n\n### Name it: you need historical state access (archive RPC) at `FORK_BLOCK`.\n\n### How to tell — 10 seconds\n\n```bash\ncast storage 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F 1 \\\n  --rpc-url \"$MAINNET_RPC_URL\" --block 23050000\n```\n\n- Returns a 32-byte value → **archive available**, ship the pin.\n- Errors with `missing trie node`, `state not available`, `header not found`,\n  or a `-32000`-family \"historical state\" message → **not archive**.\n\nRun it against the exact block you plan to pin, not an arbitrary old one. Some free tiers\nserve a *limited* archive window (last N days). Those pass a check against a recent block\nand fail six months later when the pin ages out from under you — a booby trap. If you see\nthat shape, prefer the cache-commit path below.\n\n### If it's not archive — three options, best first\n\n1. **Commit the RPC cache.** The cache dir for a pinned block is just JSON of the storage\n   slots your tests touch — usually small. Generate it once on any machine with archive\n   access, commit it under e.g. `test/fixtures/rpc-cache/`, and restore it in CI before\n   `forge test`:\n\n   ```yaml\n   - run: mkdir -p ~/.foundry/cache/rpc && cp -r test/fixtures/rpc-cache/* ~/.foundry/cache/rpc/\n   ```\n\n   CI then needs **no archive access and makes no RPC calls at all** for cached slots.\n   Fully deterministic, immune to rate limits and to archive windows closing. Cost: it must\n   be regenerated whenever the tests touch a new slot or you bump the block. Make that a\n   documented, deliberate step.\n\n2. **Switch endpoints.** Archive-capable free tiers exist. Cheapest fix if one is available\n   to you; you keep paying rate limits, but pinning cuts the volume enough that it stops\n   mattering.\n\n3. **Stop forking for these particular assertions** — see below.\n\n---\n\n## The deeper point about these three tests\n\nPinning makes them deterministic. It does not make them *good*.\n\n`assertEq(chainlinkPrice, 341_209_442_113)` at a pinned block asserts a fact about\nEthereum's history. It will hold forever, and it tests nothing about your code. What you\npresumably want to know is: *does my contract behave correctly given some price?*\n\nSo layer it:\n\n- **Unit tests, no fork.** Mock the feed and drive the inputs you care about — stale round,\n  negative answer, zero, 8-vs-18 decimals, price at the liquidation boundary.\n\n  ```solidity\n  vm.mockCall(\n      AGGREGATOR,\n      abi.encodeWithSelector(AggregatorV3Interface.latestRoundData.selector),\n      abi.encode(uint80(1), int256(3400e8), block.timestamp, block.timestamp, uint80(1))\n  );\n  ```\n\n  Fast, no RPC, no rate limit, and it covers the cases mainnet won't hand you on demand.\n\n- **Fork tests, pinned, few.** Keep a small number that assert *integration wiring* —\n  right address, right decimals, right interface, call doesn't revert against the real\n  deployment. Those are what a fork is for.\n\nThen split them in CI so the unit suite doesn't pay fork cost:\n\n```bash\nforge test --no-match-path 'test/fork/*'   # every PR, fast, offline\nforge test --match-path   'test/fork/*'    # pinned, cached\n```\n\nNet effect: fork RPC volume drops by roughly the ratio of tests you move off the fork,\nwhich is the other half of the 429 fix.\n\n---\n\n## Summary\n\n| Symptom | Cause |\n|---|---|\n| Sudden reds | Fork at `latest` → asserting on live market data that finally drifted |\n| Flaky re-runs | Each re-run = a different block = a different input |\n| Steady slowdown | `latest` is uncacheable → 100% cache miss, every slot over the wire, forever |\n| 429s | Full uncached request volume, growing, against a rate-limited free tier |\n\n**Fix:** pin `FORK_BLOCK` as a repo constant, convert tolerance assertions to exact ones,\ncache `~/.foundry/cache/rpc` in CI, move value-logic tests off the fork onto mocks.\n\n**Free-tier caveat:** the pin requires archive state at that block. Verify with the `cast\nstorage --block` command above against the block you intend to pin. If it fails, commit the\nRPC cache — that path needs no archive access in CI at all.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":550,"cache_read_input_tokens":22621,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":550},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"405091f1-ef4b-4d25-81b8-08ddcad91127","uuid":"252b09fe-0127-4cbb-afd2-0ed7f20dd6eb","timestamp":"2026-07-27T08:11:58.271Z","request_id":"req_011CdSDrWmCH4pZMBCpMRXuQ"}
